decisions.rule: Keep a flat indexed base plus at most 32 overlay patches; compact when depth exceeds 32, cumulative changed cardinality exceeds n/8, or projected overlay reads exceed one materialization.
decisions.rationale: The overlay removes full-copy mutation cost while bounded compaction prevents depth degradation; chunk objects lose on retained bytes and cold construction at the supported ceiling.

rejected.reason: Copies the complete domain for every bounded patch.
Adds block indirection and retained objects without an end-to-end win before the bounded overlay compacts.

decisions.rule: Store selected domain indexes in one sorted vector; do not retain a dense fallback until a consumer workload proves that conversion plus deterministic materialization beats the vector above 1/16 density.
decisions.rationale: Sparse selection is the bounded hot path, the vector has deterministic order and lowest retained footprint, and dense public snapshots still require output-proportional ID materialization.

rejected.reason: Dense toggles are fast but every immutable write copies the universe-sized bitset and deterministic ID output still scans the universe.
Per-entry object and hashing overhead exceeds the sorted vector on supported sparse workloads.

decisions.rule: Retain dense row-major storage and one ID-position map through the current one-million-cell ceiling; reconsider CSR/CSC only for a new workload below 5% occupancy with repeated row/column reads.
decisions.rationale: Dense addressing is constant-time, allocation-light, and wins representative construction plus mixed reads; compressed sparse storage saves empty-cell bytes but adds arrays, sorting, and binary searches.

rejected.reason: No measured CPU/allocation crossover at or above the supported 5% occupancy boundary.

decisions.rule: Build immutable preorder, postorder, child views, and Euler subtree intervals lazily once per Tree owner, then reuse them by owner identity.
decisions.rationale: The first output remains linear, repeated traversal becomes constant-time access, and lazy ownership avoids paying retained space when a view is never observed.

rejected.reason: Repeats full-domain traversal and allocation for unchanged immutable input.

decisions.rule: For a canonical well-formed source, validate the replacement and the two adjacent UTF-16 boundaries only; externally supplied text still receives a full scan.
decisions.rationale: Unchanged canonical code units are already proven, so rescanning them adds linear work without increasing safety; boundary checks cover surrogate splitting.

rejected.reason: Redundantly scans the unchanged canonical prefix and suffix.

decisions.rule: Resolve source/destination through the retained canonical index and perform exactly one unavoidable output materialization; never reconstruct the same index in the transition.
decisions.rationale: Reorder output is necessarily linear for an immutable flat snapshot, but lookup and duplicate index construction are avoidable and materially increase allocation.

rejected.reason: Performs redundant linear lookup and a second full index allocation.

decisions.rule: Reduce once with Euclidean GCD under explicit operand/result bit ceilings; cache only the fixed powers of ten 0..18 and never memoize arbitrary operand pairs.
decisions.rationale: Arbitrary rational operands have negligible reuse, while a memo retains attacker-shaped BigInt/string keys; the fixed power table is bounded and serves decimal mapping.

rejected.reason: Unbounded operand-key retention and serialization erase any low-reuse arithmetic gain.

decisions.rule: Store sorted non-overlapping half-open spans in a frozen flat vector, merge adjacency, use binary membership, and merge set algebra linearly in input span counts.
decisions.rationale: Normalization removes the overlapping-interval query that motivates an interval tree; the tree adds objects without improving logarithmic membership or linear merges.

rejected.reason: Adds node/max metadata while normalized non-overlapping spans need only binary search.

decisions.rule: Retain one deterministic frozen exception vector plus one private Set for expected-O(1) membership; return the same owner on semantic no-ops.
decisions.rationale: Membership dominates expression composition and stable output order is required; the paired bounded representations avoid persistent-set object graphs and repeated binary lookup.

rejected.reason: Saves the Set but makes every membership logarithmic and repeated algebra lookup more expensive.

decisions.rule: Use packed scan for x<=128, d>8, fewer than 128 nearest/radius queries per immutable owner, or update-heavy owners; otherwise build a balanced kd index and fall back when one query inspects more than x/2 candidates.
decisions.rationale: Low-dimensional repeated nearest queries justify kd pruning, while packed vectors win small/high-dimensional/adversarial workloads and provide the deterministic worst-case fallback.

rejected.reason: Remains the fallback but cannot be the sole representation for large low-dimensional query-heavy owners.
Requires distribution- and radius-specific cell sizing and has unstable sparse/skewed worst cases.

decisions.rule: Expose immutable finite-number records at API boundaries but evaluate at most 12 normalized placement candidates through scalar locals and materialize only the winning result.
decisions.rationale: Candidate count is fixed and tiny, so spatial indexes cannot improve complexity; scalar evaluation removes hot-loop objects, arrays, and sorting.

rejected.reason: Allocates and sorts every bounded candidate despite requiring only one minimum.

decisions.rule: Retain exactly one normalized source/query/projection generation keyed by all governing revisions; invalidate once on generation change and never retain an LRU by default.
decisions.rationale: UI access is concentrated on the active generation, so one entry removes repeated policy work while bounding heap; an LRU duplicates large projections without coherent reuse evidence.

rejected.reason: Repeats filter/sort/group/projection for access-only observations.
Retains multiple large generations with no measured active-view hit-rate advantage.

decisions.rule: incremental iff n>=1024 and repairBound(j,n)<n/2; otherwise abandon repair storage and perform one packed full rebuild.
decisions.rationale: Sixty-four-item vector blocks and spatial leaves are counted independently before the conservative copy bound; the input-derived half-rebuild ceiling prevents adversarial sparse updates from paying repair plus an uncontrolled rebuild.

rejected.reason: Retained below crossover but cannot be the sole path for small updates to large owners.
Per-item nodes and path copies exceed retained-memory and bundle budgets.

decisions.rule: incremental iff n>=1024 and repairBound(j,n)<n/2; otherwise discard the bounded attempt and rebuild packed prefix/track state once.
decisions.rationale: Blocked prefix summaries update touched tracks without eagerly shifting every placement, while the fixed bound preserves predictable fallback time and peak space.

rejected.reason: Retained for small or update-dense owners but scales with total tracks for a one-track measurement.
Fine-grained nodes increase allocation and retained heap beyond blocked summaries.

decisions.rule: Use explicit frozen normalized color records only at public/state boundaries and scalar locals through conversion matrices, transfer curves, polar transforms, and gamut loops.
decisions.rationale: The boundary remains immutable and precise while scalar internals remove transient objects; class/plugin dispatch adds dependency, allocation, and hidden extension semantics.

rejected.reason: Adds mutable identity, method dispatch, plugin closure, and one object per conversion step.
Preserves semantics but allocates intermediate records in every scalar stage.

decisions.rule: Expose reject and clip as O(1) explicit policies; implement reduce-chroma with exactly 12 monotonic OKLCH iterations and no tolerance-controlled unbounded loop.
decisions.rationale: Policy choice is semantic, not automatic; twelve iterations give a fixed work ceiling and sufficient chroma resolution while reject/clip stay allocation-free constant paths.

rejected.reason: Remains the default policy but cannot serve callers explicitly requesting perceptual gamut projection.
Remains available but may change hue/lightness relationships more than bounded chroma reduction.
